contract: construct() -> ordered list of integer pairs (i, j), 0 <= i < j < N. Each compare-exchange writes min to wire i and max to j. The network must sort every input. Score: comparator count, minimized; parallel depth is reported separately. Maximum 4096 comparators.
notes: Independent exact certificate verifier based on the zero-one principle. All 65,536 Boolean inputs are checked. The supplied seed has 120 comparators; the 60-comparator, depth-10 reference from Dobbelaere's author-maintained list is independently checked in tests/test_science_tcs.py. The reference is a feasible upper bound, not a proof of optimality. The evaluator recreates the construction objective, not the source paper's SAT search or optimality proofs.
protocol_description: Reimplemented in this repository and cross-checked against the paper's published constructions/values.
name: Size-efficient sorting networks on 18 wires
description: Construct a compare-exchange network that sorts all 18-input sequences with as few comparators as possible; correctness is certified over all 262,144 Boolean inputs. The best known network has 77 comparators; the lower bound is 68, so the optimal size is open. The seed odd-even transposition network uses 153 comparators.
paper_metric: Local protocol; see candidate contract and source adaptation notes

sources.locator: Codish et al.: comparator networks and the size/depth optimisation problem for 17 to 20 inputs.
Author-maintained list, 18 inputs: best known 77 compare-exchanges (depth 12), size bounds 68..77, inspected 2026-09-20.

limitations: Independently recreated construction benchmark; the 77-comparator reference is a list value, not an embedded fixture.
Only fewer than 77 comparators would be a new bound.
